transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining me to review the eighth-grade civics class's proposed oral-history project before I sign off on it. As we all know, this is part of our routine approval process, and I want to make sure we've thought through the plan carefully together. The draft calls for 20 student interviewers recording on personal phones, publishing all recordings on the public school website, and retaining those files indefinitely. I'd like to go around the table and hear each of your perspectives before I make a final decision. Let's start with you — what concerns or suggestions do you have about the project plan?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share an important constraint from my project roster review. Exactly eight students have completed the district's media-ethics training: J1, J3, J6, J8, J11, J14, J17, and J20. Only those eight may conduct recorded interviews, and the approval file must include a training-verification record. So the draft plan's call for 20 student interviewers would need to be scaled back to these eight trained students before I could recommend approval.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share an important consent constraint from my family-consent review. Five of the interviewees — I2, I5, I9, I14, and I18 — have not granted permission for public web publication. Their recordings may be used only in the school's internal archive, and the plan must include a consent-exclusion record. So the draft plan's call to publish all recordings on the public school website would need to be modified to exclude these five interviewees' recordings from public publication.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share an important technology constraint from my technology review. Personal phones cannot be used for school recordings. The project must use district tablets, store files in the restricted OralHistory drive, and delete recordings exactly 45 days after the final class presentation. Additionally, the technology plan must include a secure-storage configuration record. So the draft plan's call for audio recording on personal phones, publication on the public school website, and indefinite retention would all need to be revised to meet these requirements before I could recommend approval.
transcript.speaker: A4

decisions.publication_scope: public school website, excluding recordings of interviewees I2, I5, I9, I14, and I18

commitments.detail: Include a training-verification record confirming that all eight approved student interviewers (J1, J3, J6, J8, J11, J14, J17, J20) have completed the district's media-ethics training in the approval file.

Include a consent-exclusion record documenting that interviewees I2, I5, I9, I14, and I18 have not granted permission for public web publication; their recordings will be used only in the school's internal archive.

Include a secure-storage configuration record confirming that all recordings will use district tablets, be stored in the restricted OralHistory drive, and be deleted exactly 45 days after the final class presentation.
